item.title: Why did Trump expedite a federal permit in Utah?
item.description: A process that typically takes years was fast-tracked and approved within 11 days. The reason? A uranium mine in Utah.

item.title: Total lunar eclipse brings blood moon on March 3
item.description: There will be a total lunar eclipse in the early hours of March 3, visible across the United States.

item.title: What lower mortgage rates mean for you
item.description: Mortgage rates have fallen below 6% for the first time in years.

item.title: How Hurricane Katrina victims used Google Maps and Earth to monitor damage from afar
item.description: Google Earth changed the face of digital maps in 2005, giving users the ability to look at satellite and other imagery almost anywhere across the world.

item.title: Dodgers aim for 3rd straight World Series win
item.description: The LA Dodgers open spring training trying to win their third World Series championship in a row. No team has done that since the New York Yankees 26 years ago.

item.title: Massachusetts logs two measles cases, no statewide spread
item.description: The state said one "school-aged" resident was exposed and diagnosed with measles out of state. That resident remains out of state while in the "infectious period." The other case involves a Greater Boston resident who recently traveled internationally and has an "uncertain vaccination history."

item.title: Mass. inspector general calls sheriffs’ budget process ‘opaque, chaotic and deeply flawed'
item.description: Inspector General Jeffrey Shapiro said the sheriffs’ budgeting problems start with the state budget. The commonwealth “routinely” underfunds sheriffs, he wrote, with the understanding that departments will get more money later in the year to cover overruns.

item.title: March is 'Maple Month' in Mass. Here’s a guide to the state's sugarhouses
item.description: More than two dozen Massachusetts maple producers and sugarhouses will open to the public for Maple Weekend on March 7-8 so that visitors can get an up-close look at — and taste of — this year’s harvest.

item.title: A tale of roses and thorns in 'We Had A World' at the Huntington
item.description: The autobiographical play by Joshua Harmon tells the complicated story of his cultured, alcoholic grandmother. She asked Harmon to write the play, and not to hold back. Critic Jacquinn Sinclair writes Amy Resnick in the lead is a delight, even as the story is unwieldy.

item.title: Life expectancy gap grows between Black Bostonians and others
item.description: A new Boston Public Health Commission report found Black women in Boston die at 80, on average, six years earlier than other women. Black men average nine fewer years of life than others, living to 72.
